name: Utrecht University
summary: Research university in Utrecht with 10 English-taught bachelor's, from History and Media to PPE and life sciences; two select their students.

ib.text: The IB Diploma counts as equivalent to VWO. IB English A or B, SL or HL, meets every UU English level. Strictest subjects: Molecular and Biophysical Life Sciences needs Maths AA HL, Biology HL, Chemistry HL, Physics SL.

programmes.name: College of Pharmaceutical Sciences
programmes.ib: Chemistry HL, Physics SL, and Maths AA SL or AI HL. Numerus fixus: apply by 15 January via 'Farmacie' in Studielink; selection essay on a set article.
programmes.about: An English-taught track of the Pharmacy bachelor focused on discovering and developing new drugs, from the drug target and active ingredient to testing safety in patients, in classes of up to 60.
programmes.overview: The programme follows drug development from the first question to the finished product. Year one has four compulsory courses on the drug pipeline: clinical development, how drugs and the body interact, the drug and the cell, and the drug molecule. Year two adds immunopharmacology, psychopharmacology, analytical methods and pharmaceutical biotechnology, plus electives, and year three is mostly electives such as Medicinal Chemistry or Omics in Oncology. Teaching is project-based, with frequent labs run by active researchers and classes of at most 60. You carry out your own research project in year three in a research group at Utrecht University or its medical centre.
programmes.selectionNote: Numerus fixus: apply by 15 Jan 2027, questionnaire by 31 Jan. You need 3.0/5 on the questionnaire and reference, and 3.0/5 on an essay written on 1 March (online from abroad).

programmes.name: Economics and Business Economics
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL.
programmes.about: Economics and business economics studied together and applied to real questions such as climate policy or affordable healthcare; almost half the programme is optional, so you can combine it with law, geography or data science.
programmes.overview: You study macroeconomics, microeconomics, international economics and business economics, with first-year courses such as Mathematics for Economists, Accounting and Finance, Statistics and Strategy and Organisation. Year two adds econometrics and corporate finance, and year three centres on electives and an applied economics research course. Nearly half of the programme is optional: a dedicated minor can link economics to law, geography, social sciences or applied data science, and the bachelor thesis can sit between economics and that minor. You can also do an internship abroad or study at a partner university, including a year in Rome.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: English Language and Culture
programmes.about: Anglophone literatures, cultures and histories plus English linguistics, with polished language skills; from 2026 you can also take Celtic languages such as Irish and Welsh as an option.
programmes.overview: You study how English has changed and varies across groups of speakers, read literature from the English-speaking world, and train your pronunciation within a World Englishes approach. Year one includes The Sound Lab, The Writers' Lab, and literature and language history courses from the Renaissance onward. In year two you choose one of five specialisations, among them language learning and teaching, transforming texts, the social life of English and Celtic literatures and linguistics, alongside an integrated humanities track. One third of the programme is electives, and internships in the Netherlands or abroad, for example with publishers, translation agencies and schools, are possible. Year three ends with a thesis.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: Global Sustainability Science
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL, plus two of: Biology HL, Chemistry HL, Physics SL, Economics SL, Geography SL.
programmes.about: Climate, energy, resources and nature studied from local to global scale, with natural and social science courses side by side, to understand sustainability problems and help solve them.
programmes.overview: You combine mathematics, physics, chemistry and biology with management, economics and innovation to understand sustainability from local to global scale. Year one ends with fieldwork on Texel island, and in year two you pick one of five tracks, from water, climate and ecosystems to business and innovation, and work on a Global Transformation Project. In year three, track courses lead to a Consultancy Project advising real clients such as NGOs, governments and businesses, then a thesis. A quarter of the courses are electives, and you can study abroad for up to six months. Teaching draws on researchers at the Copernicus Institute of Sustainable Development.

needs.note: Two of these; Economics and Geography count as one choice.

programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: History
programmes.about: European history in a global perspective from antiquity to today, then a History track or an International Relations in Historical Perspective track from year 2.
programmes.overview: Year one surveys European history from antiquity to the present within a global frame, with research labs on source analysis and a course introducing quantitative methods. In year two you choose one of seven specialisations in two tracks: History, with themes such as political conflict in modern Europe or crises and inequality, or International Relations in Historical Perspective, including Europe in the World and conflict and security. Each ends in research seminars where you work on a historiographical debate. Year three offers electives, an internship, a minor or a semester abroad, and a thesis on a topic of your choice. Tutorials of about 20 to 25 students and excursions are central.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: Linguistics
programmes.ib: Bilingual programme: year 1 is taught in English; from year 2 two tracks are in English and one (Taal en samenleving) is in Dutch.
programmes.about: How languages are built, processed in the brain and change over time, studied with experiments, logic and a little mathematics. Year 1 is in English; one later track is Dutch-taught.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces the study of language through courses on meaning, psychology of language, morphosyntax, sociolinguistics, phonetics, language development and digital tools. In year two you choose one of three clusters: Language and Society (taught in Dutch), Language and Cognition, covering psycholinguistics and acquisition, or Language and Computation, covering corpora, computational modelling and language models, alongside an integrated humanities track. Year three has a capstone course on research and writing, electives for one third of the programme, and a bachelor's thesis. You can do an internship, with past placements at dictionary and language institutes.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: Literary Studies
programmes.about: Literature compared across languages, periods and genres, from epic to fan fiction, and in relation to other arts and media, asking what makes a text literature and what it does in society.
programmes.overview: Year one covers literary history from antiquity to the present, close reading, cultural criticism and current theoretical debates such as affect theory and environmental criticism. In year two you choose a specialisation, Literature across Borders, with postcolonial, migration and ecological themes, or Literature in Conflict, covering banned books, contested memory and dissent, and join an integrated humanities track. Year three includes The Republic of Letters, on publishing, festivals and cultural careers, electives for one third of the programme, and a thesis. You can intern at publishing houses and cultural institutions in the Netherlands or abroad.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: Media and Culture
programmes.about: Digital media, data, film, television, theatre, dance and games studied in their history, theory and social context, with workshops in theatre, music, visual arts, film and photography.
programmes.overview: Year one introduces the media landscape, storytelling, new media and digital culture, film, television, and theatre and dance, with research methods. In year two you choose one of four profiles: participatory cultures and sustainable futures, critical AI and global digital culture, media heritage and curation, or performing arts and creative technologies, together with an integrated humanities track. Year three has a research seminar, a thesis and electives for one third of the programme. Tutorial groups are small, and internships are possible at institutions such as EYE Film Museum in Amsterdam and the Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: Molecular and Biophysical Life Sciences
programmes.ib: Maths AA HL, Biology HL, Chemistry HL and Physics SL.
programmes.about: Life at the molecular and cellular level through biology, chemistry, physics and pharmaceutical science, with wet-lab work, computer practicals, programming and bioinformatics in the first 18 months.
programmes.overview: Year one lays a foundation in biology, chemistry and physics with courses such as Cell Biology, Mathematics and Programming, Physical Chemistry, Biomolecular Chemistry and Biological Physics. In years two and three you take twelve electives, at least six within the major and up to six from the whole university catalogue, organised in four themes: Genes to Organisms, Molecules and Cells, Molecules and Medicine, and Biophysics and Modelling. The programme finishes with a bachelor thesis, a research project of your own under the supervision of scientific staff.
programmes.selectionNote: No cap: meet the requirements and you are admitted. Apply in Studielink by 1 May; matching is part of enrolment (voluntary if you live abroad).

programmes.name: Philosophy, Politics and Economics
programmes.ib: Maths AA SL or HL, or Maths AI HL. Numerus fixus (75 places): application and file by 14 January 2027; grades, a test, motivation and a referee, then maybe an interview.
programmes.about: Political and economic questions studied through philosophy, politics, economics and, unusually, history, in a small intensive programme that admits at most 75 students a year.
programmes.overview: Year one has eight compulsory courses across philosophy, politics, economics and history, including Political Philosophy, Microeconomics, Macroeconomics and Comparative Democratic Institutions. Year two adds methods in qualitative research, statistics and epistemology, and one of four thematic packages: Challenges to the Welfare State, Markets and Regulators, Global Pathways to a Sustainable Future, or Democracy and its Discontents, each ending in an individual interdisciplinary research paper. Year three leaves free space for courses elsewhere or an internship, and finishes with the PPE thesis. Students have worked at banks, international organisations, embassies and ministries.
programmes.selectionNote: Selective, max 75 places: apply and send your file by 14 Jan 2027. Ranked on grades, a profile test, a written motivation and a reference; some are then interviewed.

notes: Matching (a non-binding study-choice check) is compulsory only if you live at a Dutch address on 1 May; applicants living abroad can ask to be exempted.
Binding study advice: you must earn at least 45 of the 60 first-year credits (EC) to continue.
University College Utrecht and University College Roosevelt (Middelburg) are UU colleges with their own pages, fees and deadlines.
